item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
A book publisher sent 140 copies of a certain book to a bookstore. The publisher packed the books in two types of boxes. One type of box held 8 copies of the book, and the other type of box held 12 copies of the book. The boxes were all full, and there were equal numbers of both types of boxes.

b) What fraction of the books sent to the bookstore were packed in the smaller boxes?

Answer: ____

descriptors: Another fraction or percent equivalent to 2/5 (e.g., 8/20, 14/35, 28/70, etc.)
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.scoring_notes: The term “equivalent” in the scoring guide below includes decimal fractions and percentages.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
The smaller box contains 20 tickets numbered from 1 to 20. The larger box contains 100 tickets numbered from 1 to 100.

[Image: Two boxes containing tickets]

Without looking at them, you can pick a ticket from either box. Which box would give you the greater chance of picking out a ticket with the number 17 on it?

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
